findings.title: C1 DoD turns two promise-1 homes into pointers, blocking the merge-train amendment
findings.body: Round 2 required C1 to own all four homes of promise 1. The What names PHILOSOPHY, the covenant, showrunner duty 6, and merge-train.md amended in one change set, but the DoD then says merge-train.md and duty 6 'state' the rules 'each citing PHILOSOPHY's promise 1 rather than restating it.' Spec A FR-F1.2 requires the merge-train sentence 'the owner authorizes that edit' to be amended to the craft-under-the-word rule, and register R2 names those four surfaces as homes amended together. A builder following the DoD can leave merge-train as a pointer and never change that sentence.
findings.suggestion: Grade the four homes as amended together: covenant and PHILOSOPHY carry the ruled FR-F1 shape; merge-train.md replaces 'the owner authorizes that edit' with the red-train craft rule; duty 6 carries the executable scoped-word rule. Pointers may exist in addition, not instead.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-F1.2: "The merge-train reference's 'the owner authorizes that edit' is amended to this rule by the founding-documents child." C1 DoD: "merge-train.md and showrunner duty 6 state the scoped-word rule, the red-train rule, the force-push rule, and the release rule, each citing PHILOSOPHY's promise 1 rather than restating it." R2: "promise 1's new shape in PHILOSOPHY, the covenant, showrunner duty 6, and merge-train.md amended together in one change set (C1)."

findings.title: FR-A9 bullet 2 has no coverage-map row; footer total 240 hides it
findings.body: Spec A FR-A9 has two acceptance bullets. The map lists only bullet 1 (the 1,000-line stack-or-reason rule) and then jumps to FR-A10. Bullet 2 requires the size-consideration slot to be recorded in the routed issue body beside the lane and presentation calls at the same moment the kind label is applied. C2's body names the four routing-time calls in issue-contract.md but that is not a map row, and C2's DoD does not grade same-moment recording in the issue body. The table has 239 data rows; the footer claims Total 240 and Unallocated 0. Exclusive C1 owner-column rows are five (FR-B5.1, B5.4, B6.7, F3.1, F6 n7) while the footer says C1: 6, which is how the phantom 240 is produced.
findings.suggestion: Add FR-A9 bullet 2 owned by C2. Set Unallocated to 0 only after that row exists. Correct C1 exclusive to 5 (FR-F1 stays SPLIT-F1: 5). Extend C2's DoD to require the four routing-time calls recorded together in the issue body at routing.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-A9.2: "the slot is recorded in the routed issue body beside the lane call and the presentation call, at the same moment the kind label is applied (FR-A6, FR-E1): same moment, one record plus one label." Coverage map row at FR-A9 is only bullet 1, opening "at routing, any issue estimated over 1,000 non-test lines". Footer: "C1: 6 ... Total criteria: 240. Unallocated: 0."

findings.title: C2's P2 carve-out has no fail-closed rider; C17 grades it before the door exists
findings.body: C17 owns FR-E1.3: with no stamped ladder the P2-files-free carve-out is inactive and cleared items queue at the door for the owner's word. C17's DoD records that run, and C17 sequences in Wave 1. C2 owns FR-A3.2's P2 carve-out in owner-decisions.md, sequences in Wave 2, and never states the ladder predicate. R17, which C2 quotes, also states P2 filing with no fail-closed rider. One child will ship advisor-filed P2s on an uncalibrated project; the other will test the opposite.
findings.suggestion: State in C2's What and DoD that the P2 carve-out is inactive without a stamped ladder (queue at the door, no filing). Keep C17's recorded no-ladder runs, but sequence them against C2's door home or name the helper C2 must call.
findings.evidence: C17 DoD: "A project with no stamped ladder cannot use the P2 carve-out: a recorded run shows a cleared item queued at the door for the owner's word instead of filing." C2 What: "the four tiers with the P2 carve-out amending the filing clause" with no ladder predicate. Spec A FR-E1.3: "With no stamped ladder, no band can be cited, so no P0 or P1 can be claimed and the P2-files-free carve-out is inactive." C17 sequencing: "Wave 1, after C1." C2 sequencing: "Wave 2, after C1."

findings.title: C13 claims FR-D9 in full but DoD does not grade the stay/go inventory or coverage-check failure
findings.body: Round 2 required the successor section to state FR-D9 in full. The What uses 'in full' as a table of contents ('what the successor is', tripwire, replay, sequencing, back-out). The DoD then grades only the tripwire's three conditions, the coverage replay, the sequencing rule, and the back-out as quoted, plus R23's three design questions. It does not grade FR-D9.1's stay/go inventory (writer, seat map, contracts, grounding seat, dispatch core stay; phases, gates, latches, resume, canary-as-gate, escalation ladder go). It also does not grade FR-D9.4's extra clauses: the unrun-review preventer must be runner-side telemetry, and a class without a preventer or a six-case miss parks to the owner and nothing is deleted. A vet can pass C13 with a successor note that cannot scope the later deletion.
findings.suggestion: Add DoD bullets that the successor section quotes FR-D9.1's stay/go list, that the coverage replay requires a telemetry preventer for unrun-review, and that a failed class or six-case miss parks to the owner with no deletion.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D9.1: "The four-class check and the receipt writer (FR-D8) stay; the seat map, the contracts, the grounding seat, and the dispatch core stay; the round driver's phases, gates, latches, resume machinery, the canary as a blocking gate, and the escalation ladder go." Spec B FR-D9.4: "a class without a preventer, or a case answered wrongly, parks to the owner and nothing is deleted." C13 DoD: "its successor section states the tripwire's three conditions, the coverage replay, the sequencing rule, and the back-out as quoted in this body, with the design note answering the three questions of register entry R23."

findings.title: C12 is mapped FR-D3.4 but never sends post-shrink escapes to the misses log
findings.body: Coverage map assigns Spec B FR-D3.4 to C12: post-shrink escapes in FR-D1's classes are misses-log entries so the keep-or-retire list reads catches and escapes. C12's What and DoD never mention the misses log, FR-A4, or posting those escapes. C2 owns the misses-log instrument (FR-A4) but is not this bullet's owner and does not receive a C12 seam. The mapped criterion has no build.
findings.suggestion: Add to C12 What/DoD that each post-shrink escape in FR-D1's classes is filed as a misses-log entry on C2's collector surface, and name the C2 seam.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D3.4: "post-shrink escapes in FR-D1's classes are misses-log entries (Spec A FR-A4, read at every gardening pass), so the keep-or-retire list reads catches and escapes, and the shrink cannot look healthy solely by refusing less." Coverage map owner: C12. C12 What enumerates the writer, four checks, six cases, baselines, and bump, with no misses-log sentence.

findings.title: C12 DoD does not grade the state-version bump, receipt transition note, or no-trigger refusal
findings.body: C12 owns FR-D8.10 (one state-version bump, no stored field removed), FR-D5.3 (consumer-visible shape change on the same release's transition note), and R6's writer refusal of a follow-up with no revisit trigger. The What names the bump, the transition note, and the trigger refusal. The DoD grades the import census, the six-case suite, R5 fields, hand-landed specimens, and baselines only. A vet using the DoD, the PR, and CI would not have to show the bump, the note, or a no-trigger refusal.
findings.suggestion: Add DoD bullets: the receipt fields and D1-029 ride one supported-versions bump with additions-only schema diff; the release transition note lists the receipt-shape change; a journal whose follow-up item has no revisit trigger is refused with class and artifact named.
findings.evidence: C12 What: "Ships behind the one state-version bump with no stored field removed; the transition note for the receipt shape" and "refuses a follow-up with no revisit trigger." C12 DoD bullets 1–5 never mention bump, transition note, or trigger. Spec B FR-D8.10: "this FR ships behind one state-version bump under the driver's existing supported-versions mechanism."

findings.title: C11 is mapped FR-S1.9 but does not land the native-or-marker tripwire
findings.body: Coverage map assigns Spec B FR-S1.9 to C11: after the dispatch-shell lands, a second grader/salvage fix on a marker engine proposes move-or-drop, and a second schema/adapter fix on a native engine proposes drop-or-accept-the-cost, with channel membership recorded in the C1 values annex. C11's What and DoD cover native channels, the cursor trial, the probe, substitution-or-park, scrubbing, and malformed results, and never state this tripwire. C2 reads Spec B tripwires at gardening (FR-M2.4) but does not mint FR-S1.9. The priced-benefit claim in FR-S1.7 has no measurement instrument in the owning child.
findings.suggestion: Add to C11 What/DoD the FR-S1.9 condition, its two proposals, annex channel rows as the readout source, and a C2 seam that the gardening outcome account reads it.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-S1.9: "after the dispatch-shell child lands, a second grader or salvage fix ... on any engine still on the marker channel proposes ... move that engine to a native channel, or drop the engine. ... On an engine already on its native channel, a second schema or adapter fix after landing ... proposes at the next pass either dropping the engine or accepting the cost in the record." Coverage map owner: C11. C11 What has no tripwire sentence.

findings.title: C10 DoD does not grade FR-S1.4's transition note or the one-time consumer tell
findings.body: C10 owns FR-S1.4 and quotes R8, which requires no alias window, a release-note transition note listing every changed argument and result shape, a stale-caller refusal that names the replacement, and the registered consumers told once (weekly-eats write path named). The DoD grades allowlist refusals, MOVE echo-or-drop, effort echo, liveness cache, generated entry doc, forfeit-ledger removal, and the three keep-or-retire entries. It does not require the transition note or the consumer tell. A vet can pass C10 with a silent shrink.
findings.suggestion: Add DoD: the release note's transition note lists every dropped, renamed, or newly required argument and the result-shape change; a recorded stale-caller refusal names the replacement; the PR body records the one-time tell to registered consumers.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-S1.4: "The refusal a stale caller meets names the replacement or the new requirement ... the release note that ships the shrink lists every changed argument and result shape in one plain transition note; and the advisor tells the registered consumers once." C10 DoD entry-doc bullet: "the doc declares the shell's variance envelope and states the refusal-streak condition" with no transition note.

findings.title: C10 queues three keep-or-retire entries that C6's census DoD never consumes
findings.body: R25 and FR-S1.8 move the stdout cap, salvage paths, and dirty-tree probe from contract rows to keep-or-retire entries with citation-based conditions. C10 (Wave 1) DoD allows those three entries to 'exist in C6's doc or [be] queued for it in the PR body.' C6 (Wave 2) DoD grades only 'every census-row component of the machinery map' and never mentions C10's queue. If those three are not already census rows, C6 will not land their citation-based conditions and C10's queue dies in a PR body.
findings.suggestion: Make C6 consume C10's three queued entries by name (stdout cap, salvage paths, dirty-tree probe), each with a citation-based condition, whether or not they appear on the machinery map.
findings.evidence: C10 DoD: "the three keep-or-retire entries exist in C6's doc or are queued for it in the PR body." C6 DoD: "The keep-or-retire reference doc lists every census-row component of the machinery map with all six fields of register entry R16 filled." Spec B FR-S1.8: "The stdout cap, the salvage paths, and the dirt probe become keep-or-retire lines with citation-based conditions."

findings.title: Canary leaves the gate with no child grading the historical telemetry confirmation
findings.body: Spec B FR-D8.7, mapped to C12, requires the certification child to confirm from the canary record since 2026-08-30 that no case the plant caught would pass telemetry, before the plant leaves the gate. C13's DoD lets a fizzled probe certify on engagement telemetry and is the child that removes the canary as a blocking gate. C12's What/DoD never mention that historical confirmation. The leave and the precondition are split with no seam, so the gate can lift without the record check.
findings.suggestion: C12 DoD: record the 2026-08-30-forward canary census (plant-caught cases vs telemetry). C13 DoD: the canary leaves only when that C12 receipt is attached to the PR.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D8.7: "The certification child confirms from the canary record since 2026-08-30 that no case the plant caught would pass telemetry, before the plant leaves the gate." C13 DoD: "The planted-defect canary no longer blocks certification: a review whose probe fizzled certifies when telemetry shows the seat engaged, recorded in a dry run." C12 body has no canary-record confirmation.
